title: Ringed direct image commutes with derived completion, with its unit normalization
statement:
Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_X),R_X)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_Y),R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small sites: its inverse image $f^{-1}$ preserves finite limits and is left adjoint to $f_*$, and its ring map is $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$, where the $R_T$ are sheaves of commutative rings. Let $\mathcal J_Y\subset R_Y$ be an ideal sheaf locally generated by finitely many sections, and let $\mathcal J_X\subset R_X$ be the ideal generated by its image. Use the unbounded module derived categories $D(R_T)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $Rf_*:D(R_X)\to D(R_Y)$ be total right derived module direct image, computed with K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; module direct image and its ring action are as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction].

Write $\Lambda_T:D(R_T)\to D(R_T)$ for the left-adjoint reflection into locally derived $\mathcal J_T$-complete complexes, with unit $\eta_T$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-extended-cech-completion-model]. Here locally complete means that for every site object $U$ and $a\in\mathcal J_T(U)$ the derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom_{R_T|_U}(R_T|_U[1/a],M|_U)$ is zero; localization is sheafified sectionwise localization [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then $Rf_*$ sends locally derived $\mathcal J_X$-complete objects to locally derived $\mathcal J_Y$-complete objects. For every $M\in D(R_X)$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\gamma_{f,M}:\Lambda_Y(Rf_*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*(\Lambda_X M).$$
It is the unique arrow satisfying
$$\gamma_{f,M}\circ\eta_{Y,Rf_*M}=Rf_*(\eta_{X,M}).$$
There is no boundedness or constructibility hypothesis on $M$, no Noetherian hypothesis on the ring sheaves, and no assumption that $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Construct a left adjoint L to the supplied Rf in the independently sized derived categories. Obtain the closed tensor-Hom adjunctions from the ringed derived closed-structure theorem. The augmented Cech tensor-pullback result gives finite type on IX. Choose global augmented Cech models by the existing model theorem, then apply the tensor-pullback result to those supplied models.

Construct the natural inverse-transpose augmentations from the Cech units using the adjunction counits; their normalization follows from the Hom-equivalence inverse law. Take right adjoints of the tensor comparison. The two composite adjunctions have the same left adjoint, so right-adjoint uniqueness gives δ:Rf⋙CechHomY≅CechHomX⋙Rf. Apply the Hom-equivalence formula for that unique isomorphism to σY followed by the counit of L⊣Rf. Naturality and both transpose equations give precisely unitY≫δ=Rf(unitX). The canonical Cech units are natural.

The Cech reflector properties and the supplied reflector bijections give unique unit-preserving natural isomorphisms from the supplied completion functors to their Cech models. Conjugate δ by them. The conjugate has the required unit equation. For a complete source object its reflector unit is invertible, by the reflection bijection; therefore its target unit is invertible by the unit equation. The latter identifies its direct image with a complete object. Local completeness is invariant under isomorphism since each defining test is the zero-object property after applying two functors. Finally injectivity of the target reflection bijection gives uniqueness among all arrows.

proof_origin.place: Tags 099J and 0A0G; shorter augmented Cech tensor-pullback argument followed by right-adjoint uniqueness and reflector uniqueness. Categorical glue proved by X5.
